summary: Iteration 26 (worker-status diagnostic endpoint + verbose [radar-worker] logging) end-to-end verified on preview against https://trial-saas-hub.preview.emergentagent.com. 12/12 pytest cases passed AFTER fixing one CRITICAL bug in the new endpoint (offset-naive vs offset-aware datetime subtraction in /worker-status would 500 *exactly when a job is running*, i.e. the moment the user needs to hit it in production). Endpoint shape matches spec (worker.{alive,ready,started_at,queue_size,motor_pool_size=10,jobs_*,current_job_*,last_job_*}, mongo_running_jobs[], mongo_recent_jobs[], server_time). Label format 'enrich limit=L llm=B pw=B job=<8hex>' confirmed on both current_job_label and last_job_label. Singleton invariant intact: across 5-cycle enrich/cancel + 12-parallel hits + 50-record enrich + double-enrich 503 guard + login/auth + verdict-PATCH suite, only 1 'thread READY' log line on the current backend process (31 queued, 31 started, 30 done — no respawn). Tier C core + 503 guard + verdict PATCH + login latency all green.

minor.issue: ORIGINAL BUG: line 1706 of saas_radar.py did `(now - updated_at).total_seconds()` where `now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)` (offset-aware) but Motor returned `updated_at` as offset-naive on this DB, raising `TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`. The 500 fired ONLY when mongo_running_jobs had at least one row — i.e. exactly when a job was running, which is the only scenario where the diagnostic endpoint is interesting. Reproduced under TestTierCRegression: 2/12 parallel hits to /worker-status returned 500 during an active enrich. FIX APPLIED IN THIS ITERATION: coerce naive updated_at to UTC-aware via `updated_at.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` before subtraction. After fix, all 12 parallel hits return 200 and all telemetry tests pass. Recommend reviewing parallel datetime handling in `mongo_recent_jobs` (currently we only emit ISO strings there so no math is done, OK) plus the rest of saas_radar.py for the same naive-vs-aware bug class.

Editing any /app/backend/*.py file while a radar worker job is active causes uvicorn --reload to fire and the worker subprocess to hang mid-shutdown (in-flight httpx coroutines on the worker loop are not cancelled). Required `sudo supervisorctl restart backend` once during this iteration after fixing saas_radar.py. NOT a production issue — production does not run with --reload.

action_items: REVIEW the timezone-aware coerce I added at saas_radar.py worker-status `mongo_running_jobs` block — confirm the same defensive pattern is applied anywhere else updated_at/created_at from Mongo participates in arithmetic. Production Atlas may also return naive datetimes (depends on the codec_options used by AsyncIOMotorClient); without this fix the diagnostic endpoint would 500 in production exactly when a job is running, defeating its purpose.
critical_code_review_comments: BUG (fixed in this iteration, saas_radar.py line ~1706): mongo_running_jobs stale_secs computation crashed with `TypeError: can't subtract offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes` whenever the running list was non-empty. The endpoint is specifically designed to be hit *during* a job, so this was a 100%-failure-rate bug on the headline diagnostic. Coerced naive→UTC-aware before subtraction.

worker.status() telemetry counters (_jobs_submitted/started/completed/failed) are read+written from two threads (API request thread vs worker thread) without locks. Python int increments are not atomic in CPython under the new free-threaded build (3.13t+); under standard GIL-Python the read is fine, but counters CAN appear non-monotonic during a race window (read jobs_submitted before _start, write +=1 inside, etc). RECOMMENDATION: switch to itertools.count() iter().next() pattern or threading.Lock-guarded mutations if you ever upgrade to free-threaded Python.
Status snapshot returns 14 keys via plain dict assembly — fine for now, but as fields grow consider Pydantic model so OpenAPI docs auto-update and clients get typed contracts.

Log lines '[radar-worker]' prefix is consistent across QUEUED/START/DONE/FAILED/READY/EXITING — easy to grep, good. One missing prefix: line 302 'SaaS Radar worker did not become ready within 5s' should also be `[radar-worker]` prefixed for grep consistency.

Label format 'enrich limit=L llm=B pw=B job=<8hex>' is documented implicitly via the f-string at line 1773; if any future caller changes the format the tests will fail (they regex-match it). Consider extracting a helper `_enrich_label(job_id, req)` so the format lives in one place.

The fix applied to saas_radar.py line 1704-1713 MUST stay in place — if reverted, /worker-status will 500 the moment a job starts. The user's whole reason for adding this endpoint is to hit it mid-lockup on production; if the endpoint itself crashes mid-running-job, the diagnostic strategy is defeated. Recommend production redeploy of saas_radar.py with this fix BEFORE the user attempts the next lockup reproduction.
rca of the issue: In server-style code that stores datetimes via Motor/PyMongo on MongoDB Atlas, returned datetimes are by default offset-naive (PyMongo's default codec_options has tz_aware=False). The /worker-status implementation computed `(datetime.now(timezone.utc) - updated_at).total_seconds()`. Because `updated_at` was naive but `now` was aware, Python raised TypeError and the endpoint 500'd. The bug surfaced only when mongo_running_jobs was non-empty (i.e. there was a row matching {status:'running'}), so a quick idle smoke-test would PASS while real production diagnostics would FAIL — exactly the kind of bug that survives review. FIX: defensive `if updated_at.tzinfo is None: updated_at = updated_at.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` before subtraction. Same class of bug should be hunted everywhere `datetime.now(timezone.utc) - <mongo-returned-datetime>` appears. Long-term: configure AsyncIOMotorClient with tz_aware=True in saas_radar.py worker init (line 311) and remove all naive-coerce code paths.
